Rod.cl_def_summary: One of the two photoreceptor cell types of the vertebrate retina. In rods the photopigment is in stacks of membranous disks separate from the outer cell membrane. Rods are more sensitive to light than cones, but rod mediated vision has less spatial and temporal resolution than cone vision.

BC.cl_def_summary: A bipolar neuron found in the retina and having connections with photoreceptors cells and neurons in the inner plexiform layer.

AC.cl_def_summary: Interneuron of the vertebrate retina. They integrate, modulate, and interpose a temporal domain in the visual message presented to the retinal ganglion cells, with which they synapse in the inner plexiform layer. They lack large axons.

HC.cl_def_summary: A neuron that laterally connects other neurons in the inner nuclear layer of the retina.

RGC.cl_def_summary: The set of neurons that receives neural inputs via bipolar, horizontal and amacrine cells. The axons of these cells make up the optic nerve.

MG.cl_def_summary: Astrocyte-like radial glial cell that extends vertically throughout the retina, with the nucleus are usually in the middle of the inner nuclear layer.
MG.granularity_note: MG/Astro granularity limitation (D001 measured): In current MG entries {RLBP1,GLUL,SOX9,VIM,S100B}, 4/5 genes have best-class non-MG or no specificity in reference system (GLUL MG1908/Astro2099, SOX9 reverse, VIM shared, S100B MG≈0); true MG-dominant genes (e.g., RLBP1 MG1018/Astro70) rely on RPE exclusion. Astro entry strong anchors only GFAP(lfc3.56)+S100B. Two entries share VIM/S100B → n_shared count at reading end misleading (Q2::22 measured: three-way judged MG while v2_prod cell-level 100% Astro). Repair route = MG entries re-derived with D001 focus (candidates see KB5V3 report §5, v6 separate card); this annotation does not touch panel.

Micro.cl_def_summary: A transcriptomically distinct central nervous system macrophage found in the parenchyma of the central nervous system. Marker include CD11b-positive, F4/80-positive, and CD68-positive.

RPE.cl_def_summary: An epithelial cell of the retinal pigmented epithelium.

BC.cl_def_summary: A bipolar neuron found in the retina and having connections with photoreceptors cells and neurons in the inner plexiform layer.

RB.cl_def_summary: A bipolar neuron found in the retina that is synapsed by rod photoreceptor cells but not by cone photoreceptor cells.  These neurons depolarize in response to light.

DB1.cl_def_summary: An OFF diffuse bipolar cell that makes synaptic contact with both L/M and S-cone photoreceptors and only minimal contact with rod photoreceptors.

DB2.cl_def_summary: An OFF diffuse bipolar cell that predominantly connects to ON parasol cells and lateral amacrine cells. This cell contains a large number of synaptic ribbons and a small axon arbor area.

DB5.cl_def_summary: A diffuse bipolar 5 cell typically contacts 7–8 cone photoreceptors. The number and thickness of its dendritic processes are intermediate between those of a diffuse bipolar 6 cell (less dense and thinner) and a diffuse bipolar 4 cell (denser and thicker).

FMB.cl_def_summary: An OFF bipolar cell with a small dendritic tree that provides most of the triad-associated basal (flat) contacts at cone pedicles.

IMB.cl_def_summary: An ON bipolar cell with a small dendritic tree that forms most of the central (invaginating) elements opposite the synaptic ribbon at the cone triad.

ON-BC.cl_def_summary: A bipolar neuron found in the retina and having connections with photoreceptors cells and neurons in the inner half of the inner plexiform layer. These cells depolarize in response to light stimulation of their corresponding photoreceptors.

OFF-BC.cl_def_summary: A bipolar neuron found in the retina and having connections with photoreceptors cells and neurons in the outer half of the inner plexiform layer. These cells depolarize in response to light to dark transition.

AC.cl_def_summary: Interneuron of the vertebrate retina. They integrate, modulate, and interpose a temporal domain in the visual message presented to the retinal ganglion cells, with which they synapse in the inner plexiform layer. They lack large axons.

HC.cl_def_summary: A neuron that laterally connects other neurons in the inner nuclear layer of the retina.

H1.cl_def_summary: A horizontal cell with a large cell body, thick dendrites, and a large dendritic arbor.

H2.cl_def_summary: A horizontal cell with a small cell body, thin dendrites, and small dendritic arbor.
